x: Youngsters, and new scoring members of our County team were Nick Milsum and Terry Clark who finished 8th and 10th respectively. Both grand efforts and Ben Clark, an old Belgravian, must have been proud to see his son winning his first County Medal.
Special mention must be made of Nick Milsum, now in the R.A.F., who finished the course in 59 minutes 6secs. and won the sealed handicap together with his R.W.A.
Our younger members are showing that they are not to be outdone by setting a new Surrey County record in the one mile Walk, Terry Clark taking first place in 7m. 14s and Nick Milsum 2nd in 7m. 21s.

Terry Clark won this trophy in the very good time of 40m.04s. with Trevor Luck 2nd in 41.07 and Nick Milsum 3rd in 41.24. Although it is difficult to get a big field for this race as it coincides with the age for National Service, I hope there will be a few more next year.

Nick Milsum who was having his last race before joining the R.A.F. the following Monday, decided to let off steam and clocked his best time for five miles with 39mins. 35secs. and with a generous mark of 6.30. won the handicap.
The Junior Walk Record had stood to Jack Rutland for exactly 20 years until Terry Clark won the Surrey Junior Championship in the time given above. Nick Milsum was also inside the old record.

At the same meeting we had two entries in the Junior one mile walk with Terry Clark and Nick Milsum. They both walked exceptionally well with good, fair walking and were a credit to our Walking Section.

August Bank Holiday 6th August proved a good day for our walkers when two teams entered the open 6 miles race at Chertsey which starts and finishes on the track. We were pleased to see Nick Milsum home on leave and Wally Emery who has started again. We look forward to seeing him during the winter.

In an Inter-County Junior Match on 11th August, Surrey v Essex, Nick Milsum was 2nd in 7m. 34.6s. Whilst some of our runners may not have been present at Inter-Club meetings, they have had engagements elsewhere.

Ray Middleton, home from Ireland, walked well to finish 6th in 41m.21s., Dave Stevens (individual) was 7th, Nick Milsum 9th and Terry Clark, who walked a blinder on the last lap, was 12th and Trevor Luck 13th.

Our three, Ray Middleton, Nick Milsum and Ray Switzer pursued a steady course together for the first half of the race and then began their advance through the field, with Middleton proving himself our best man on the day, finishing in 14th position.

Nick Milsum had a bad time, but fought back well to regain lost ground near the finish. At four miles Eric moved away and Stan fell back to third, but not for long however, as over the last mile he closed right up again and Eric just got home by 14 seconds.

We lost Nick Milsum and Terry Clark of our first team men, but their turn will come. Nick was particularly unfortunate for he was our fourth man, on the last lap and, in the view of many, walking splendidly as he came through the field.
